scope.note: Statement scope reviewed against the pinned main theorems: the pure spin-one antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model with coupling one on even periodic rings; a separate theorem covers odd open chains with equal endpoint fields h = 3/5. The topological conclusion concerns boundary-selected subsequential local limits, without asserting global uniqueness of all infinite-chain ground states. This is a statement review, not proof verification.

originalQuestion: Haldane’s 1981 preprint predicted a qualitative split: isotropic antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chains with integer spin have a positive excitation gap, while half-odd-integer chains are gapless. Spin one is the smallest positive integer-spin case.
modernQuestion: For the pure spin-one Hamiltonian on even periodic rings, does the gap between the ground energy and the next distinct energy have a strictly positive lower limit as the number of sites tends to infinity? A separate formulation fixes positive magnetic fields at the endpoints of odd open chains.
questionDifference: The early continuum argument predicted behavior across spin values. The reported periodic theorem fixes spin one, a pure bilinear interaction, coupling one and even rings. The boundary companion fixes h = 3/5 on odd open chains. A gap for the AKLT interaction, which adds a squared interaction term, does not by itself answer either question for the pure model.
questionPlainLanguage: A chain of quantum spins has a lowest possible energy. Does exciting a spin-one antiferromagnetic chain always cost a minimum amount of energy, even as the chain becomes arbitrarily long?
questionSummary: Can a quantum chain grow forever without its energy gap closing?
claimSummary: a spin-one gap for even rings and fixed boundary fields
questionFormal:
At each site, take the standard spin-one operators, with $\mathbf S_j^2=2I$. In units where the antiferromagnetic coupling is one, the pure periodic Hamiltonian is

$$
\begin{aligned}
H_N&=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\mathbf S_j\cdot\mathbf S_{j+1},\\
\mathbf S_N&=\mathbf S_0.
\end{aligned}
$$

Take even $N\ge4$. Let $E_0(N)$ be its ground energy and $E_1(N)$ the next distinct energy. Write $\gamma_N=E_1(N)-E_0(N)$. The question is

$$
\Delta_1=\liminf_{\substack{N\to\infty\\N\text{ even}}}\gamma_N>0.
$$

A positive gap at each fixed size does not establish this uniform limit. For odd open chains, the companion instead studies $H_L(h)=\sum_{j=-L}^{L-1}\mathbf S_j\cdot\mathbf S_{j+1}-h(S^z_{-L}+S^z_L)$ on $2L+1$ sites at the single field $h=3/5$, with no bond joining the endpoints.
whyItMatters:
A spectral gap describes the energy needed to leave the ground state. The difficult word is **uniform**: a positive gap in every finite chain can still shrink to zero as the chain grows. Haldane’s prediction showed that changing the spin from a half-integer to an integer could change this large-system behavior, even with the same nearest-neighbor interaction.

The question also connects to how quantum phases are distinguished. A solvable spin-one model supplied a rigorous gapped example; later work identified symmetries that protect its topological character. For the pure Heisenberg chain, proving the gap and proving a topological implication are separate tasks. Boundary conditions specify which question each theorem addresses.
illustrativeExample: For **two spin-one sites**, the total spin $s$ is $0$, $1$ or $2$, and $q=\mathbf S_1\cdot\mathbf S_2$ has eigenvalue $[s(s+1)-4]/2$. The AKLT bond adds $q^2/3$. The diagram gives these exact local spectra, using the same energy scale and no added constant. Neither two-site gap determines the gap of an arbitrarily long chain.
historicalHook: An unpublished 1981 prediction became a question about an energy gap that must survive every larger chain.
whatAIClaims:
The periodic manuscript reports a unique ground state for every even $N\ge60$ and an explicit positive lower bound on its gap. For every even $N\ge2304$, it reports $\gamma_N>\log(20)/784$, hence $\Delta_1\ge\log(20)/784>0$. This concerns the pure bilinear spin-one model.

The companion treats $2L+1$ open sites with equal endpoint fields $h=3/5$. It reports $E_1(L,3/5)-E_0(L,3/5)>\log(10)/392$ for every $L\ge960$. Applying Tasaki’s theorem, it then obtains index $-1$ for every boundary-selected subsequential local limit.
whatRemainsOpen:
These statements do not cover every spin, odd periodic rings or arbitrary endpoint fields. The lower bounds do not determine the exact bulk gap; White and Huse’s familiar estimate near $0.4105$ is numerical. Free open ends have their own low-energy behavior.

The boundary corollary does not establish convergence of the entire ground-state sequence, uniqueness among all infinite-volume ground states, or the additional global uniqueness assumption used in Tasaki’s half-chain corollary. The reported proofs and finite computational certificates have not been independently assessed by this project.
attribution: F. D. M. Haldane formulated the integer versus half-integer prediction. Lieb, Schultz and Mattis supplied the earlier spin-one-half obstruction; Affleck and Lieb extended the half-odd-integer branch. Affleck, Kennedy, Lieb and Tasaki proved a gapped example with a different interaction. Numerical evidence, perturbative stability and topological classification developed alongside the pure-model gap question. These are distinct contributions in a selected history, without an exhaustive priority claim.

contributors.name: Elliott H. Lieb, Theodore Schultz and Daniel Mattis
contributors.contribution: Established the 1961 spin-one-half low-energy result that forms a precursor to the integer versus half-integer distinction.

contributors.name: F. D. M. Haldane
contributors.contribution: Predicted the contrasting low-energy behavior in a 1981 preprint and the 1983 published field-theory papers.

contributors.name: Ian Affleck and Elliott H. Lieb
contributors.contribution: Proved the half-odd-integer obstruction in their 1986 class of antiferromagnetic chains.

contributors.name: Ian Affleck, Tom Kennedy, Elliott H. Lieb and Hal Tasaki
contributors.contribution: Constructed a valence-bond spin-one model with a rigorously established spectral gap.

contributors.name: Steven R. White and David A. Huse
contributors.contribution: Used density-matrix renormalization to estimate the pure-model gap and characterize effective spin-one-half degrees of freedom at open ends.

contributors.name: Dmitry A. Yarotsky
contributors.contribution: Established perturbative stability around the AKLT interaction.

contributors.name: Frank Pollmann, Erez Berg, Ari M. Turner and Masaki Oshikawa
contributors.contribution: Explained the symmetry protection of the odd-spin Haldane phase.

contributors.name: Hal Tasaki
contributors.contribution: Developed a local-twist index and proved the pure Heisenberg chain’s nontrivial index conditional on a uniform boundary-field gap.

uncertainty: The 1981 date comes from Haldane’s preserved transcription, uploaded in 2016; it is the earliest explicit prediction identified here, not a claim about the first circulation day. Publisher abstracts and bibliographic records were inspected for the 1961, 1983, 1986, AKLT and 1993 milestones; those full original proofs were not reviewed. Topological introductions and statements were inspected. The 2026 main theorems and boundary corollary were reviewed for scope, without executing their certificates or assessing their proofs or independent acceptance. This selected account omits many experimental, numerical and rigorous developments.

events.title: A low-energy obstruction for spin one-half
events.description: Lieb, Schultz and Mattis establish a spin-one-half low-energy result. Integer spin is not forced into the same obstruction.
events.relationNote: A precursor to the contrast, not a proof of an integer-spin gap.

events.title: Haldane predicts the integer-spin gap
events.description: The preserved July 1981 preprint predicts a singlet ground state with gapped excitations for integer spin, contrasting with half-integer behavior.
events.relationNote: The continuum argument supplies the integer-spin prediction.
events.uncertainty: Date supplied by the later transcription.

events.title: The prediction reaches print
events.description: Haldane’s published field-theory paper connects spin chains to a nonlinear sigma model and distinguishes integer from half-integer behavior.
events.relationNote: Published development of the earlier prediction.
events.uncertainty: The 1981 text is an earlier identified formulation.

events.title: Affleck and Lieb prove the other branch
events.description: Their theorem excludes a unique gapped infinite-chain ground state for half-odd-integer spin under the paper’s assumptions.
events.relationNote: Extends the rigorous obstruction; does not settle spin one.

events.title: A related spin-one model has a rigorous gap
events.description: Affleck, Kennedy, Lieb and Tasaki construct a valence-bond model with a spectral gap. The extended 1988 account develops the rigorous example. Its interaction differs from the pure Heisenberg bond.
events.relationNote: A rigorous realization of gapped integer-spin behavior for a related Hamiltonian.

events.title: Numerical evidence sharpens the pure-model picture
events.description: White and Huse estimate the bulk gap as 0.41050(2) and identify effective spin-one-half degrees of freedom at open ends.
events.relationNote: Studies the pure-model spectrum and boundary behavior.
events.uncertainty: A numerical estimate does not establish a uniform rigorous lower bound.

events.title: The AKLT gap survives small perturbations
events.description: Yarotsky’s perturbation theory establishes stability around the AKLT interaction, rather than a complete path to the pure Heisenberg point.
events.relationNote: Extends the rigorously controlled model neighborhood.
events.uncertainty: First preprint 2004; timeline uses the journal year.

events.title: Symmetry explains a topological distinction
events.description: Pollmann, Berg, Turner and Oshikawa describe how particular symmetries protect the odd-spin Haldane phase.
events.relationNote: Adds a phase-classification question alongside the gap question.
events.uncertainty: First preprint 2009; timeline uses the journal year.

events.title: A local twist gives a rigorous index
events.description: Tasaki defines a Z₂ index for unique gapped spin-one ground states with specified symmetries, invariant under smooth deformation.
events.relationNote: A rigorous index framework distinguishes AKLT and trivial phases.

events.title: For the pure chain, topology follows if the gap holds
events.description: Tasaki proves index −1 for the boundary-selected infinite-chain state, assuming a uniform gap on odd open chains with endpoint fields.
events.relationNote: The boundary gap becomes a precise sufficient hypothesis.

events.title: The OpenAI release: periodic and boundary gap claims
events.description: OpenAI reports a uniform gap for even periodic spin-one rings and, separately, odd open chains with endpoint field h = 3/5. The companion applies Tasaki’s theorem to boundary-selected local limits.
events.relationNote: The periodic theorem addresses the original gap prediction in a fixed formulation; the companion supplies the boundary hypothesis.
events.uncertainty: Statement scope reviewed; proofs and certificates not independently assessed.
